svg.title: Thirty Days to a Controlled Pilot
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-thirty-day-launch-sprint; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Thirty Days to a Controlled Pilot; subtitle: Build evidence and repayment discipline before pursuing annual scale.; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Four consecutive weekly milestones cover days 1–30. The canonical first-deal window is 1–3 months, so this sprint targets operational readiness rather than requiring a completed deal by day 30. Provider availability, issuer terms, and warehouse acceptance must be verified directly.; caption: Expand only after an entire commitment-to-cleared-cash cycle reconciles. A successful import, pending reward, or initiated ACH does not establish realized profit.; stages: label: Map counterparties and obligations; value: Days 1-7 — establish the three-ledger operating foundation; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Verify buying-group identities and current terms, collect receiving instructions, and document tax treatment. Create separate wholesale, rewards, and treasury accounts in the operating ledger. Record issuer closing dates, due dates, limits, and restrictions.; label: Build matching and stress tests; value: Days 8-14 — prove every transaction can be reconstructed; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Load permitted card and bank exports into a reconciler keyed by order and settlement identifiers. Test duplicate rows, split ACH, missing parcels, reward reversals, and a 60-day payout delay. Require reserved cash to survive the stressed schedule.; label: Execute a bounded pilot; value: Days 15-21 — submit a small order only if ready; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Use one verified commitment, insured shipment, documented purchase terms, and full repayment coverage. Capture portal attribution only where reseller use is permitted. If onboarding remains incomplete, rehearse with synthetic ledger entries rather than forcing a purchase.; label: Reconcile and set expansion limits; value: Days 22-30 — close evidence gaps before increasing exposure; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Match any received inventory acceptance and cleared ACH to the original commitment; retain open items as receivables rather than assumed cash. Compare actual contribution with the order model, pay obligations on time, and sweep only genuine surplus. Continue the pilot into months two or three if needed.

text.title: Thirty Days to a Controlled Pilot
text.tspan: Thirty Days to a Controlled Pilot

circle.title: label: Map counterparties and obligations; value: Days 1-7 — establish the three-ledger operating foundation; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Verify buying-group identities and current terms, collect receiving instructions, and document tax treatment. Create separate wholesale, rewards, and treasury accounts in the operating ledger. Record issuer closing dates, due dates, limits, and restrictions.

text.title: Days 1-7 — establish the three-ledger operating foundation

circle.title: label: Build matching and stress tests; value: Days 8-14 — prove every transaction can be reconstructed; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Load permitted card and bank exports into a reconciler keyed by order and settlement identifiers. Test duplicate rows, split ACH, missing parcels, reward reversals, and a 60-day payout delay. Require reserved cash to survive the stressed schedule.

text.title: Days 8-14 — prove every transaction can be reconstructed

circle.title: label: Execute a bounded pilot; value: Days 15-21 — submit a small order only if ready; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Use one verified commitment, insured shipment, documented purchase terms, and full repayment coverage. Capture portal attribution only where reseller use is permitted. If onboarding remains incomplete, rehearse with synthetic ledger entries rather than forcing a purchase.

text.title: Days 15-21 — submit a small order only if ready
text.tspan: Days 15-21 — submit a small order only

circle.title: label: Reconcile and set expansion limits; value: Days 22-30 — close evidence gaps before increasing exposure; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Match any received inventory acceptance and cleared ACH to the original commitment; retain open items as receivables rather than assumed cash. Compare actual contribution with the order model, pay obligations on time, and sweep only genuine surplus. Continue the pilot into months two or three if needed.

text.title: Days 22-30 — close evidence gaps before increasing exposure

Assumptions: Four consecutive weekly milestones cover days 1–30. The canonical first-deal window is 1–3 months, so this sprint targets operational readiness rather than requiring a completed deal by day 30. Provider availability, issuer terms, and warehouse acceptance must be verified directly.
